correctness.rationale: The independent Laplace check is 1/(2d²) times [1/(w+a)-2/(w+a+d)+1/(w+a+2d)], which equals the product of the three original transforms. The window is real and causal, so with T=|τ| the substitution t=u+T/2 gives the prefactor e^(-aT-iπνT)/(4d⁴) and a one-sided integral. Setting z=e^(-du) gives the extra 1/d and the integral of z^(s-1)(1-z)²(1-ρz)² over [0,1], analytic for Re s>0. Expanding yields beta terms B(s,3)-2ρB(s+1,3)+ρ²B(s+2,3); their common denominator is D and the numerator is 2[(s+3)(s+4)-2ρs(s+4)+ρ²s(s+1)], exactly 2P_ρ. In s+3 the three coefficients are (1-ρ)², (1-ρ)(1+5ρ), and 6ρ(1+ρ); all are positive for 0<ρ<1, so the real parts of both roots are negative in that variable. Hence real ν (Re s=2a/d) cannot be a zero. The five P_ρ(-j) are positive in the same range, so no poles cancel. The discriminant has sign of ρ²-14ρ+1, with the unique admissible root 7-4√3; at that root the double zero is -2-√3. For smaller ρ, the shifted s+4 roots are real with positive sum and product, giving -4<s<-3. For larger ρ they are conjugate nonreal in s. At T=0, ρ=1 gives the nonzero constant 12, so no finite zeros. The affine map s(ν) is invertible over C and the exponential prefactor has no finite zeros or poles, yielding exactly the stated meromorphic census and preserving multiplicities.
residual_risks: The recorded numerical integral tests start from the closed form for the convolution and corroborate the rational formula only on sampled parameters; the Laplace identity independently validates that window. Neither the calculation nor the theorem covers arbitrary unrelated triples or larger cascades. Complex zeros belong to the continuation, not the real-frequency integral.

value.rationale: This is a tractable but non-equal-rate instance of a specific distinct-rate problem identified in primary time–frequency literature. It settles the entire real ambiguity plane for a natural first higher cascade and describes how the continuation zeros appear, collide and split at finite delay. The exact shift and noncancellation show why the complex transition does not obstruct real zero-freeness. This gives a concrete benchmark for a broader theory, not just a single parameter example.
residual_risks: Practical significance beyond the exact time–frequency classification, or a criterion for arbitrary positive rate triples, is not established.
